analyst_view.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) meet Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, where UEFA moved the game for security reasons; most of the crowd should still be Besiktas fans. The trip went badly: bad weather stopped the team plane landing in Batumi, it diverted to Rize and the squad finished the journey by road on Wednesday evening, and Vincenzo Italiano's press conference was cancelled. Fanatik reports Italiano plans to limit Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes before the Galatasaray derby, with Hyeon-gyu Oh and Vaclav Cerny set to start; Umit Akdag is banned, Agbadou stayed home with a swollen knee and Miretti is still out. Hapoel are without first-choice keeper Ofir Marciano, Lucas Ventura and Dan Biton (all counted) and play a league game two days later. Danish referee Morten Krogh's low card rate is already in the numbers; I trim goals and shots on target a little more than yesterday because Besiktas' best finishers now look likely to start on the bench.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 2.3 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.2%) and for Marciano missing in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%). Since yesterday Fanatik reports Oh and Cerny should start with Vlahovic and Trossard kept fresh for the derby, and the squad arrived late after a diverted flight and a road trip, neither of which the numbers can see, so I go a little lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should still have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and changes up front alter who finishes moves more than how often they reach the byline, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh's low card rate (2.9 a game). Krogh's crew was also diverted by the weather and came in by road from Trabzon, but he is still the named referee, and with a mostly Besiktas crowd and a home side expected to dominate nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas, already nudged for recent form. Besiktas should keep shooting often against a weak defence with a reserve keeper, but a rotated front line after a tiring journey may take a little off their volume, so I go slightly lower, to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, 7.7 for Besiktas, already lifted for sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and trimmed for Hapoel (-5.8%). With Vlahovic and Trossard, Besiktas' best finishers, now expected to start on the bench, the quality of their chances should drop a little, so I go to about 10.0.
